history.hpi: 8-year-old with type 1 diabetes diagnosed at age 5. Mother reports he received his scheduled rapid-acting insulin dose at lunch today but skipped his usual afternoon snack while at a friend's house. He came home tremulous, sweaty, and irritable, telling his mother he feels 'really hungry and shaky.' Mother checked his home glucometer, which read 42 mg/dL, and called 911.
medications: Insulin aspart (rapid-acting) per sliding scale with meals
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch at school approximately 1 hour prior to onset of symptoms; skipped afternoon snack
history.events: Mother noticed him trembling and sweaty after school, checked his home glucometer reading 42 mg/dL, and called 911

scene.location: Single-family home, kitchen; patient seated at the table with his mother
scene.bystanders: Mother present, reports he took his lunchtime insulin but skipped his afternoon snack
visualCues: Home glucometer on the counter reading 42 mg/dL
Insulin pen and used lancet in a sharps cup nearby
Backpack and half-eaten granola bar on the table
Patient visibly trembling with beads of sweat on his forehead

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find an 8-year-old male seated at the kitchen table, conscious, tremulous, and diaphoretic. He is anxious but able to speak in full sentences and follow commands.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and strong bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Fine tremor noted in both hands, strength otherwise intact
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really shaky and hungry, my tummy feels weird."

transitions.condition: Crew confirms blood glucose is 42 mg/dL, recognizes symptomatic hypoglycemia, and administers weight-based oral glucose since the patient is conscious with a patent airway.

phases.name: Oral glucose given
phases.description: Crew confirms hypoglycemia with a glucometer check and administers oral glucose gel dosed to the patient's weight, appropriate for a conscious patient able to protect his airway.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing symptomatic hypoglycemia (BGL 42 mg/dL) in a conscious, airway-protecting patient, the crew administers weight-based oral glucose per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and strong bilaterally
otherFindings: Oral glucose gel administered and tolerated
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That tastes weird but I still feel shaky."

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose level with glucometer
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms hypoglycemia (BGL less than 60 mg/dL) before treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Oral glucose gel 12.5 g PO (25 kg × 0.5 g/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Conscious patient with a patent airway: Glucose, oral (in form of glucose tablets, glucose gel, tube of cake icing, etc.) Pediatric Dosing: 0.5–1 g/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Oral glucose is first-line for a conscious, airway-protecting pediatric patient.

transitions.if: BGL recheck still low after oral
transitions.condition: Repeat blood glucose after oral glucose remains 45 mg/dL and the patient's tremor/diaphoresis has not resolved, prompting escalation to IV dextrose.
Crew does not recheck blood glucose or reassess mental status after the oral dose, missing persistent unresolved hypoglycemia.

phases.name: IV dextrose given
phases.description: Repeat blood glucose remains low and symptoms persist after oral glucose, so the crew establishes IV access and administers weight-based dextrose per protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: Repeat BGL of 45 mg/dL with continued tremor and diaphoresis after oral glucose indicates persistent hypoglycemia requiring IV dextrose.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: IV access established, radial pulses strong

expectedActions.shortAction: Recheck BGL after oral dose; confirm still 45 mg/dL with persistent symptoms
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Repeat check of blood glucose level if previous hypoglycemia and mental status has not returned to normal
expectedActions.rationale: Identifies that oral glucose alone did not resolve hypoglycemia, justifying escalation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Dextrose 12.5 g IV as 125 mL D10% (25 kg × 5 mL/kg = 125 mL)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Maximum field pediatric dosing: 0.5–1 g/kg of 10–25% dextrose IV 5–10 mL/kg of 10% dextrose (newborns 2 mL/kg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based IV dextrose corrects persistent hypoglycemia when oral treatment is insufficient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Use D10% concentration rather than higher-concentration dextrose for this pediatric patient
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dextrose 10% can be safely used in all ages of patient. Dextrose 10% works as effectively and quickly as other concentrations
expectedActions.rationale: D10% is equally effective and safer than more concentrated dextrose solutions in pediatric patients.

transitions.condition: Repeat blood glucose rises above 80 mg/dL, tremor and diaphoresis resolve, and the patient returns to his baseline mental status.

phases.name: Improved, transport
phases.description: Blood glucose and mental status have normalized following IV dextrose. The patient is reassessed and prepared for transport given his history of symptomatic hypoglycemia.
phases.triggerCondition: After IV dextrose corrects the BGL above 80 mg/dL and symptoms resolve, the patient is reassessed and transported per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot better now, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vitals and mental status; transport given continued symptomatic hypoglycemia today
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If hypoglycemia with continued symptoms, transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.rationale: A symptomatic pediatric hypoglycemic episode requiring IV dextrose warrants transport rather than field release.

phases.name: BGL recheck skipped
phases.description: After oral glucose, the crew does not recheck blood glucose or reassess mental status. Persistent, unrecognized hypoglycemia continues, and the patient becomes more tremulous, tachycardic, and confused.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew omits the post-treatment glucose recheck and mental status reassessment, missing that hypoglycemia has not resolved.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Increasing tremor, slower to follow commands

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize worsening hypoglycemia; recheck BGL and reassess mental status immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Repeat check of blood glucose level if previous hypoglycemia and mental status has not returned to normal
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed recheck allows unrecognized hypoglycemia to worsen toward altered mental status and seizure risk.
